description: 源图核对中的六条实例；其余条目仍在逐图转录。

rules.name: Acetoacetic ester synthesis — C2 monoalkylation demo

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis

rules.structure_evidence: PDF page 56 rendered scheme and explanatory text; alkylating agent is represented generically as R2-X, instantiated here with bromoethane for a deterministic replay.

reported_scope: C2 alkylation of acetoacetic esters with primary or secondary alkyl, allyl, or benzyl electrophiles
exclusions: This record does not encode the subsequent hydrolysis/decarboxylation step

limitations: The book scheme uses a generic R2-X drawing; the bromoethane instance is constructed for replay and is not claimed as a reported substrate example.
Leaving-group atom map 10 is intentionally deleted from the product; strict SMIRKS audit remains pending.

rules.name: Arbuzov reaction — phosphite to phosphonate

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: trialkyl phosphite plus primary alkyl halide

rules.structure_evidence: PDF page 70 gives the generic trialkyl phosphite / primary bromide or iodide transformation and its SN2 description; methyl phosphite and bromoethane instantiate R groups for replay.

reported_scope: mainly primary alkyl bromides and iodides
exclusions: Aryl and alkenyl halides are described as unreactive; secondary and tertiary halides may eliminate or fail

limitations: The R groups are constructed from the generic scheme and are not claimed as a specific reported substrate example.
Leaving-group and displaced alkoxy maps are deleted; strict SMIRKS audit remains pending.

rules.name: Aza-Wittig reaction — imine formation

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: iminophosphorane plus carbonyl to Schiff base

rules.structure_evidence: PDF page 78 shows an iminophosphorane reacting with a carbonyl compound to release triphenylphosphine oxide and form a Schiff base.

reported_scope: aldehydes and ketones; intramolecular heterocycle formation is discussed
exclusions: The upstream azide-to-iminophosphorane Staudinger step is not included

limitations: PPh3O and leaving groups are not represented as products; constructed small-molecule reactants are used for replay.

rules.name: Baeyer–Villiger oxidation — ketone to ester

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis

rules.structure_evidence: PDF page 82 gives the ketone-to-ester/lactone transformation with a peroxyacid and describes migratory aptitude and retention at the migrating center.

exclusions: Regioselectivity and migratory aptitude are not encoded by this minimal graph rule

limitations: The peroxide is a minimal oxygen donor proxy rather than a specific peroxyacid; regioselectivity and acid by-product are not represented.

rules.name: Williamson ether synthesis — alkoxide plus primary haloalkane

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Williamson ether synthesis example: ethoxide plus ethyl chloride

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered scheme on printed page 484 depicts ethoxide displacement of a primary haloalkane to give diethyl ether; the replay preserves that depicted small-molecule example.

reported_scope: primary alkyl halides or sulfonates with alkoxides/phenoxides
exclusions: tertiary electrophiles favor elimination; steric and competing nucleophiles are not encoded

limitations: The source example is represented as a minimal graph edit; chloride is deleted and counterions/solvent are omitted.
This is RDKit reaction SMARTS, not a claim of strict Daylight SMIRKS compliance.

rules.name: Sonogashira coupling — aryl bromide plus terminal alkyne

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 424 shows an aryl/vinyl halide coupled with a terminal alkyne under palladium/copper catalysis; bromobenzene plus acetylene is the deterministic R-group replay.

reported_scope: aryl or vinyl halides with terminal alkynes
exclusions: aryl chlorides and hindered substrates may require specialized catalysts; homocoupling is not encoded

limitations: The book scheme is a general R-group transformation; bromobenzene/acetylene instantiates the generic groups for replay and is not claimed as a reported substrate pair.
Bromide is deleted; catalyst, base, and copper acetylide are not represented.

rules.name: Michael addition — ethyl cinnamate plus diethyl malonate

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Michael (1887) ethyl cinnamate plus diethyl malonate

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered historical example on printed page 286 shows ethyl cinnamate reacting with diethyl malonate under sodium ethoxide in ethanol to give the beta-addition product; the encoded replay preserves the displayed carbon skeleton and three ester groups.

reported_scope: stabilized carbon nucleophiles adding to activated alkenes or alkynes
exclusions: regioselectivity, protonation state, and competing 1,2-addition are not encoded

limitations: The rule encodes the single historical example and omits sodium ethoxide, ethanol, proton-transfer steps, and stereochemical mixture.
This is RDKit reaction SMARTS; strict SMIRKS dialect review remains separate.

rules.name: Wittig olefination — phosphorane plus aldehyde

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Wittig reaction general scheme, methylidene ylide plus aldehyde

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 486 shows a phosphorous ylide adding to an aldehyde or ketone to form an alkene with triphenylphosphine oxide extrusion; methylene triphenylphosphorane and acetaldehyde provide a deterministic replay.

reported_scope: aldehydes and ketones with stabilized, semi-stabilized, or nonstabilized phosphorous ylides
exclusions: E/Z selectivity and ylide preparation are not encoded

limitations: The replay instantiates the generic R groups with methylene triphenylphosphorane and acetaldehyde; it is not claimed as a specific synthetic application substrate pair.
Phosphine oxide, counterions, stereochemical composition, and ylide generation are not represented.

rules.name: Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling — arylboronic acid plus aryl bromide

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Suzuki cross-coupling general scheme and synthetic applications

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 448 depicts an organoboron reagent coupling with an organic halide under Pd(0)/base; phenylboronic acid plus bromobenzene is used as a deterministic aryl–aryl replay.

reported_scope: aryl, alkenyl, alkyl and alkynyl boron reagents with aryl/vinyl halides or triflates
exclusions: boron and halide by-products, catalyst, base, and stereochemical retention are not encoded

limitations: The aryl pair is a constructed replay of the general scheme, not a claim about one of the complex total-synthesis substrates shown on printed page 449.
Boron, oxygen, bromide, catalyst, base and ligand atoms not retained in the coupled product are intentionally omitted.

rules.name: Mitsunobu reaction — alcohol esterification with carboxylic acid

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Mitsunobu alcohol plus carboxylic acid esterification

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 294 explicitly shows an alcohol and carboxylic acid converted to an ester under phosphine/azodicarboxylate conditions; ethanol and benzoic acid are used for deterministic replay.

reported_scope: primary and secondary alcohols with acidic O-, N-, S- or C-nucleophiles
exclusions: inversion, stereochemical configuration, and reagent by-products are not encoded in this minimal acyclic replay

limitations: The source scheme is general; ethanol/benzoic acid instantiate the R groups and do not claim to reproduce a particular reported experiment.
Triphenylphosphine, azodicarboxylate, water/hydrazine by-products, and stereochemical inversion are omitted.

rules.name: Grignard reaction — organomagnesium addition to a ketone

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: Grignard reagent addition to carbonyl compound

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 188 explicitly shows one equivalent of R–MgX adding to a ketone to give a tertiary alcohol after work-up; acetone and methylmagnesium bromide provide a deterministic replay.

reported_scope: aldehydes and ketones; one or two equivalents determine secondary or tertiary alcohol formation
exclusions: acidic functional groups, moisture, and stereochemical/diastereoselective effects are not encoded

limitations: The substrate pair is a constructed minimal replay of the general scheme, not a claim about a specific total-synthesis example on printed page 189.
Magnesium bromide, solvent, work-up, side reactions, and stereochemical outcome are not represented.

rules.name: Aldol reaction — ketone enolate addition to an aldehyde

source.book: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis
source.scheme: classical aldol addition of ketone enolate to aldehyde

rules.structure_evidence: The rendered general scheme on printed page 8 shows an enolate or carbonyl donor adding to an aldehyde/ketone to give a beta-hydroxycarbonyl compound before optional dehydration; acetone and benzaldehyde provide a deterministic replay.

reported_scope: aldehydes and ketones; preformed enolates and several metal enolates
exclusions: dehydration, enolate geometry, diastereoselectivity, and competing self-condensation are not encoded
selectivity: E/Z enolate geometry can affect syn/anti ratio

limitations: The acetone/benzaldehyde pair is a constructed replay of the general scheme, not a claim about a particular reported substrate pair.
Only the beta-hydroxycarbonyl addition product is represented; dehydration to the alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl and stereochemical outcome are omitted.
